To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the two trihexyl(tetrade- clyl)phosphonium chiral ionic liquids are excellent solvents for a diverse array of organic solutes, with the trihexyl(tetri- decyl)phospho- nium (1S)-(-)-10-cam- phorsulfonate ionic liquid being the better solvent of the two.

(a) the trihexyl(tetrade-cyl)phosphoniium ionic liquids are nonpolar solvents, and (b) both ionic liquids are capable of hydrogen bond donating and accepting interactions, and (c) the trihexy(tetradecy)phosphonium cation is capable of hydrogen bond accepting interactions, but is not capable of hydrogen bond donation interactions.

the two ionic liquids have very different properties, as reflected by their different sets of ion-specific equation coefficients, and that these differences are consistent with the different structures and different physical-chemical properties of their anions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the determination of infinite dilution activity coefficients for a large number of organic solutes in two trihexyl(tetrade-cyl)phosphorium ionic liquids, and with the subsequent interpretation of the measured data in terms of a solvation parameter model.
the development of a predictive method for the calculation of gas-to-ionic liquids partition coefficients, and the determination of the corresponding ion-specific equation coefficients.

the development and application of an equation coefficient-based general solvation parameter approach to the interpretation of experimental data for infinite dilution activity coefficients and gas and water to ionic liquid partition coefficients of solutes dissolved in a pair of trihexyl(tetrade-cyl)phosphoium ionic liquids, and the calculation of ion-specific Abraham solute descriptors for these two ionic liquid anions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the two trihexyl(tetrade-cyl)phosphorium ionic liquids studied are both highly hydrophobic, and that they are both more hydrophobic than the corresponding trihexyl(tetredecyl)phosphonum bromide ionic liquid studied earlier.
the ionic liquids investigated in this study are very effective solvents for the extraction of solutes from water.
both the chiral anions and the chiral cation are solvated by a combination of hydrogen bonding, dipolarity/polarizability, and dispersion interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Abraham general solvation model is able to provide a quantitative description of the solvation properties of these ionic liquids, with the exception of a small but significant contribution from the ion-specific anion term.
the trihexyl(tetrade-cyl)phosphinium cation and the two anions have very similar ion-specific equation coefficients, but that the two anions differ in their ability to hydrogen bond with solutes.

the trihexyl(tetrade- clyl)phosphonium chiral ionic liquids studied here are more selective than the corresponding achiral ionic liquid for polar and polarizable solutes and less selective than the corresponding chiral ionic liquid toward apolar solutes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the l-lactate anion has a stronger tendency to hydrogen bond to the organic solute than does the (1S)-10-camphilorsulfonate ion.

, for the two trihexyl(tetrdecanyl)phosphium ionic liquids studied, the l-lactate anion gives rise to an ionic liquid that has a more hydrophobic and a less polar character than the (1S)-10-camhorsulfonate ionic liquid.
both anions are capable of solvating a wide variety of solutes in a similar way to water.
